absent: Full definitions of pool, page and block structures beyond fields observed in fragments.
Numeric values of freed and allocated poison markers and their stability.
Coherent allocation and free semantics and their failure modes.
Device pools file layout and read format.
Page allocator, slab and reclaim behaviour outside routed fragments.
Values of temporary slot count, per slot page count, slot base and protection constants.
Early versus late fixmap installation semantics and paging init ordering.
Layout of executable range and info structures and meaning of alignment, fallback and shadow flags.
Tree iteration and store semantics and large page alignment rationale.
Direct map and memory attribute update failure modes.
Device resource matching and release ordering guarantees.
Block count sizing rationale in the self test and timing output stability.

findings.text: Creation of a coherent block pool validates its inputs and links the new pool into the device pool list, publishing a device file for the first pool of a device and undoing the linkage on failure. A null device, a non power of two alignment, an empty or oversized size, or an undersized or non power of two boundary is rejected with a null result.

Destruction tolerates a null argument, unlinks the pool from the device list under two mutexes, removes the device file when the last pool goes away, reports a busy pool and skips releasing coherent pages while still freeing page descriptors and the pool object.

Allocation pops a free block under the pool spinlock, and when empty drops the lock to obtain a coherent page, then retakes the lock to carve the page into blocks and pop again. On success it records the device address for the caller, runs a corruption check and optionally zeroes the block.

Free validates the address pair under the pool spinlock and only on success returns the block to the free list and decrements the active count, otherwise leaving the pool unchanged after reporting the error.

Managed creation allocates a device resource holder for a pool, creates an ordinary pool and attaches the holder to the device on success or releases the holder on failure. Managed destruction releases the matching resource by device and pool identity and warns on mismatch. Release simply destroys the stored pool.

Early mapping offers device, normal, read only and raw protection variants over one shared slot engine, plus matching unmap entry points and a chunked physical to virtual copy helper. One build configuration implements them as identity conversions and no operation unmaps.
Executable memory provides a restore operation that transitions a byte range to read only executable with page granularity derived from the supplied size.

Requested block size is raised to at least the link header size and rounded up to the alignment, with zero alignment treated as one. The per page allocation is the larger of block size and page size, an empty boundary defaults to the allocation and is otherwise capped at the allocation.

The free list is a singly linked chain headed by the pool, with pop removing the head and counting an active user and push inserting at the head while recording the device address. Page initialisation appends the newly carved chain in front of any existing free blocks and updates block and page counters.

One build scans a block beyond its header for the freed poison value, reports corruption with a dump and otherwise marks the whole block allocated unless allocation time initialisation is requested, while page initialisation prefills the whole allocation with the freed value. The alternate build performs no check or prefill and only zeroes on free when free time initialisation is requested.

Device address lookup walks pages in list order and treats an address as belonging to the first page whose start is not above it and whose distance from the start is below the per page allocation, returning null when no page matches.

Carving walks an offset from zero while a full block fits in the allocation, skipping forward to the next boundary when a block would straddle it, assigning increasing virtual and device addresses to successive blocks linked in order.

Slot allocation refuses to run late in system state with a warning, requires a free slot, rejects zero length or wrapping ranges and page counts above the per slot limit, and aligns the physical range outward to page boundaries before installing one fixmap entry per page.

Unmapping locates the slot by exact virtual address equality, requires the supplied length to equal the recorded length and the address to lie inside the fixed map area, then clears one fixmap entry per page covering the page aligned span and marks the slot free.

The early copy helper iterates until the requested length is consumed, each iteration limiting the chunk so that page offset plus chunk fits in the maximum mappable chunk, mapping only the aligned cover, copying the slice and unmapping the same span before advancing both pointers.

One executable allocation path requests a ranged allocation with kernel flags and caller address, retries in a fallback range when configured and the first attempt fails, warns on total failure, and on success optionally creates a shadow allocation that frees the range on failure. The alternate path delegates to a plain allocation of the same size.

Direct map validity is updated in strides derived from the area page order, tracking how many pages were updated so that a failure restores the opposite validity over exactly the completed prefix before returning the error.

Global pool list changes hold a registration mutex outside a list mutex, with creation adding under both and removing under both if publishing the device file fails, and destruction removing under both before conditionally removing the device file after dropping the inner mutex.

The per pool spinlock is taken with interrupt state saved for free list and counter updates in alloc and free paths, and is explicitly dropped across the sleeping coherent page allocation before being retaken to install the new page.

A single mutex serialises the busy and free trees and the pending free counter, is statically initialised with the trees bound to it as external lock, and is held across the whole background reclamation scan.

A pool links pages and device membership through list heads, carries name device size boundary allocation node counters for active blocks total blocks and pages plus a free head and locks, while a page carries a virtual base a device base and a list node and a block carries a device address and a next link.

The test defines a pair of device address plus virtual pointer and a parameter triple of size alignment and boundary, with a constant table of six combinations from tiny to page sized and one unaligned size with page boundary, plus globals for the active pool the fake device and its mask.
Early mapping keeps three parallel boot data arrays indexed by slot for current mapping address recorded length and slot base virtual address, each sized by the number of temporary slots.
The executable cache holds a mutex, busy and free trees and an unsigned pending free count documented as protected by that mutex.
Two file scope pointers describe executable range configuration, one pointing at the active info and one holding a default info object, both marked read only after initialisation.

A block is free while linked from the pool head, becomes active when popped with the active counter incremented, and returns to free only after validation with the counter decremented. A new page starts unlinked, is prefilled, is carved into a chain, is spliced in front of the free list and is appended to the page list.

Each slot starts empty, becomes occupied with recorded address and length on map, and returns to empty on matching unmap. A global flag selects early versus late fixmap primitives, setup initialises base addresses with a once warning on reuse, and a leak check counts slots still occupied.

A managed pool is unregistered until creation attaches its holder to the device, remains reachable through device resource matching by pool identity, and is destroyed exactly once when its resource is released either explicitly or at device teardown.

Boot entry points initialise slot bases, flip the paging initialised flag, enable a debug flag from a boot string that adds warnings with stack dumps on map and unmap, and provide a weak protection adjustment hook returning its input by default.

The self test registers a fake device with no release action and no dma operations, installs a wide mask, iterates over the parameter table running many allocate free cycles per entry with rescheduling, then deletes and releases the device. Its exit routine does nothing.
Destroying a pool with active blocks reports busy and deliberately leaks all coherent pages of that pool while still unlinking and freeing descriptors, so callers must quiesce allocations first.

Freeing an address with no containing page reports bad dma and freeing a block already on the free list reports already free, in both cases without changing the pool. A block whose bytes after the header differ from the freed poison triggers a corruption report plus a dump of the whole block.

Late mapping primitives unconditionally abort, while slot exhaustion, allocation failure, oversized mapping and unmap of unknown or length mismatched addresses only warn and return null or do nothing, leaving the caller to handle the failure.

Background reclamation only frees areas whose length and start are both large page aligned, looking up the virtual area for each candidate before restoring direct map validity and freeing. Forcing write access clears execute before enabling write and propagates the first failure without attempting the second step.
The pool self test repeats each parameter case one hundred times.
The largest single early mapping span equals the per slot page count shifted by page shift.
Deferred free delay for executable cache entries is ten milliseconds converted to timer ticks.
The pending free marker is a single bit at position page shift minus one.
Executable memory log lines carry a fixed textual prefix identifying the subsystem.
